intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Let's walk through how computer vision grew up - from brain cells to block worlds to deep nets.

intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Four stops: history's order, Marr's stages, ImageNet's categories, and what CNNs really are.

L1U1.speaker: aya
L1U1.text: Three big moments, three different decades. Can you line them up in time?

L1U2.speaker: aya
L1U2.text: Marr imagined vision as a ladder of sketches, from raw light to full 3-D shape.

sourceRefs.quote: Stages of Visual Representation, David Marr, 1970s

L1U3.speaker: aya
L1U3.text: ImageNet sorted millions of pictures into neat families - can you find where each word belongs?

L1U4.speaker: aya
L1U4.text: CNNs are famous now, but were they really an overnight idea?

outro.speaker: aya
outro.text: From cat brains to face detectors to CNNs - vision's history is longer than it looks, and none of it happened overnight.

intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Now let's size up the course itself - what it covers, how it's graded, and the fine print on late days.

L2U1.speaker: aya
L2U1.text: Some tasks get named right away, others show up a bit later on the list - can you tell which is which?

L2U2.speaker: aya
L2U2.text: The course zooms in on one big problem, but the bigger dream is much wider than that.

L2U3.speaker: aya
L2U3.text: Three grading pieces, three different weights - match them up.

L2U4.speaker: aya
L2U4.text: Here's a tricky case with late days - think about what the policy does and doesn't cover.

outro.text: Image classification is the course's anchor, but the grading and late rules are just as important to get right.
